why: Defects found by audit and NOT yet fixed. This exists because the session that found them had no queue, so priority became whatever was most recent and thirty real findings lived only in a transcript. A finding here is not a claim that something is broken in general — each names a file, a line, and the input or condition that exposes it, so it can be reproduced or refuted. Drain in order of severity. A fixed entry moves to `fixed` with the commit that closed it; a refuted one moves to `refuted` with what disproved it.

open.what: computeLog2 is a six-branch ladder that cannot return 0, so a constant buffer with true entropy zero reports 1 bit/byte. And :339 prints 'approaching 8 bits/byte' directly under measured 4.0000 — unreachable by construction, since H <= log2(n) caps a 16-byte sample at 4.
open.reproduce: all-zero input -> repo reports 1.0000, true value 0.0000
open.fix: handle p = 1 explicitly; state the sample-size ceiling instead of an unreachable target

open.what: entropy_never_decreases is (List.range 9).all (fun t => t <= t + 1) — a Nat tautology with S as the identity, so no input can falsify it. vacuousGaps() cannot see it because it splits at paren depth 0 and this sits at depth 1 inside the lambda.
open.reproduce: vacuousGaps() returns 0 against a theorem that is vacuous by inspection
open.fix: state entropy as a function that can decrease, and teach vacuousGaps to descend into lambdas

open.what: hardware_above_landauer carries 10^32 on the RHS where the wing's unit implies 10^17, so the theorem stays true if silicon were 10^15 times worse than it is. The js mirror carries the SAME literal, so the cross-check confirms agreement and not correctness.

The school is chaotic and unusable and must be rebuilt from scratch against a stated information architecture: name/mission, ENROLLMENT requirements and application, grade levels and courses, academic calendar and dates, tuition or free-public-school status, technology requirements, student handbook and policies, teacher and counsellor information, FAQ, contact and technical support, and news/announcements/clubs/events.

open.where: src/mcp.ts (189 tools, 38 categories) against the 68 skills carried by theorems in src/theorems/generated.ts
open.what: A theorem is meant to be a hook and hooked at once — reachable from the live API through the skill it carries. Only 18 of 68 skills are reachable from any tool name or category; 50 are ORPHANED, including sequence, involution, z9-ring, z7-rosette, clay-reflection, foundational, neuro and science-pairs. Theorems carrying those skills are sealed, witnessed and served by nothing.
open.reproduce: intersect the distinct theorem skills with MCP tool names and categories; 18 match, 50 do not
open.fix: Serve skills as a dimension rather than adding 50 tools by hand: one tool that takes a skill and returns its theorems, its handles and its ESCO mapping. src/school-apis.ts already wires ESCO for exactly this and is currently referenced by nothing (0 call sites). That closes the orphan set in one computed surface instead of fifty authored ones — and a finder should then assert the intersection, so a new skill cannot arrive unserved.

open.where: package.json (38 npm scripts, 30 gate steps), src/scripts (159), src/scripts/guard.ts (29 finders), src/mcp.ts (189 tools)
open.what: The automation surface has grown past what a reader can hold, and several entries do overlapping work. MEASURED: 10 of 38 npm scripts are a single dist call adding nothing but a name — gen:captain-claims, axioms, reconcile, security, develop, probe:apis, guard, mcp:drive, state, x. And FIVE separate entry points all answer one question, what is the state of this ledger: measure, rosetta, exercise-dormant, discover, trial-protocol. Three overlapping catalogues describe the same work: 30 gate steps, 29 guard finders, 38 npm scripts.
open.reproduce: count them; then note that measure.js already registers six measurements behind one call, which is the shape the other four should fold into
open.fix: FOLD, do not add. The good precedents are already here and each REPLACED N entry points with one: gate-all took 30 chain steps into a single concurrent pass, measure --all took six one-liners into one receipted call, searchAll took six libraries into one search, handleOf took three derivations of a handle into one, exercise-dormant took 32 unrun scripts into one roster. Register rosetta, exercise-dormant, discover and trial-protocol INTO measure so there is one command, one receipt, and one obvious way in; retire the thin npm wrappers in favour of the x dispatcher, which the scripts finder already asks for. NOT a sixth entry point. The aggregate is the defect, not any single addition — 27 files were added in one session, each defensible alone.
open.caution: A count of scripts no npm script names is NOT a count of dead scripts: 72 lean-* wing emitters are discovered from disk by lean-all by design, and others are invoked by siblings. Measure invocation, not naming, or this fold will delete working code.

open.where: src/mcp.ts and src/mcp-http.ts — the tool catalogue served to every client
open.what: Loading the MCP catalogue costs about 43,637 tokens PER CONNECTION (174,548 bytes for 190 tools), and 130,851 bytes of that — 75% — is tool DESCRIPTIONS. The median description is 646 bytes and the longest is 2,849. Every agent pays this before it can do anything, on every connection, whether or not it uses a single tool.
open.reproduce: JSON.stringify the catalogue name/description/inputSchema triples and measure; then sum description bytes alone
open.fix: Cap the catalogue description at roughly 200 bytes — one sentence saying what the tool does and when to reach for it — and move the reasoning behind it to a resource the agent fetches ONLY if it calls the tool. Capping saves an estimated 23477 tokens per connection. Then a finder asserts the cap, or it regrows: the four longest descriptions are all RECENT additions (school_apis, oeapi, grow_life, rosetta_legs), which is how it got here.
open.caution: The prose in those descriptions is genuinely load-bearing here — it is where honest scope is stated, and this project states scope constantly. Do not delete it; MOVE it. A capped description that drops the honest-scope clause would trade tokens for exactly the property the ledger exists to hold.

fixed.what: BigInt(1 << (state.scale * 2)) with scale 16 wraps to 1 in JS 32-bit bitwise, so every probability is wrong and every quantum receipt is the SAME constant, independent of plaintext.
fixed.closed_by: Both delegated to the verified simulator (distribution, marginal) instead of recomputing, AND the key moved out of a phase into the basis state. The overflow was real but never the cause: hadamardX and hadamard have the identical distribution, so the key was unreadable by any measurement. Receipts 1/4 distinct became 4/4; measureMessage returns bits instead of zeros. src/tests/quantum-message-encoding.test.ts
